reading.body:
This facility publishes 3.75 MW of critical load UPS capacity in Richardson, Texas, which ranks it at the lower end of the 18 data centers in the state with disclosed power figures. Texas has 468.41 MW of published IT capacity across those 18 facilities, making this campus roughly 0.8 percent of the state's disclosed base. The operator has published a street address and square footage, enabling verification.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 3.75 MW IT load would support approximately 94 racks; at 20 kW per rack, a denser mixed-workload standard, roughly 188 racks. These figures assume the published UPS capacity reflects usable IT load, though the operator does not clarify the fraction of critical load dedicated to compute versus supporting infrastructure. The facility's 100,807 square feet of technical space suggests room for growth beyond current published power.

The campus holds compliance credentials in data security (SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS, HITRUST CSF), government standards (NIST 800-53, ITAR), and security frameworks (SSAE 18), which qualify it to host regulated workloads but do not indicate current tenant mix or specialization in GPU-intensive workloads. No power source, grid interconnection details, cooling approach, or maximum available capacity beyond the UPS rating are published.
